newsitem.title: USA: Most US spot resids flat to down, NYH loses ground.
newsitem.headline: Most US spot resids flat to down, NYH loses ground.

text.p: Most U.S. spot residual fuel prices were steady to lower again Thursday in moderate trade, with mild East Coast weather still pressuring New York Harbor grades, while fuel at the Gulf seemed well supported.
"New York feels a tad weaker. Utilities are not burning a lot, but it's been hot in the Gulf, so it's a little better supported there," said one cash trader.
But utilities said the recent slide in resid has made fuel more competitive with natural gas.
"We're burning oil where we can, but there's not a lot of demand," said one New England utility source.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent slipped more than a quarter to the $15.75-16.00 a barrel area, with August one percent paper down slightly to $16.05-20 with softer crude. Traders said September paper was quoted at $16.00-10.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour remained the best supported grade, holding unchanged at about $17.50 on reports a New York utility's buy program for August would tally about 850,000 barrels.
High sulphurs in New York, pressured by soft bunkers, slipped slightly, with 2.2 percent now talked at $14.75-15.00.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were steady to modestly firmer, with three percent still at $14.50-75, while one percent edged up a quarter to $15.50-75, traders said.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate August gas prices again were relatively unchanged Thursday in the low-$2.40s/mmBtu, or $15.25 a barrel equivalent. August gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed a few cents to $2.22/mmBtu, or $13.99 a barrel.
